correctness.rationale: The directed-incidence criterion follows by examining every possible third graph edge between two selected incidence edges in a bipartite subdivision. Directed length-two walks force isolated reciprocal pairs; the remaining arcs separate into source-to-target blocks. Missing arcs and unused vertices can be added, so maximal blocks are complete and cover the remaining vertices; all other additions are excluded except the one-by-one exceptional case. The factorial count normalizes unordered pairs and ordered source/target partitions without duplication. The sharp extrema and parity follow algebraically. Raw-graph exhaustive subset comparisons through n=5 and direct validation of constructed families through n=8 agree with each claimed coefficient; these finite results are corroboration, not the unrestricted proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The published families include unsubdivided complete multipartite graphs and trees, while once-subdivided complete graphs contain many cycles and are not among those claimed exact families. General upper/lower bounds cannot determine the cardinality polynomial. The current result concerns all maximal rather than only maximum packings.

originality.rationale: The claim classifies and enumerates every inclusion-maximal edge-open-packing set in every once-subdivided complete graph. The inspected foundational and subsequent edge-open-packing research treats maximum sizes, complexity, tree algorithms and bounds, not the complete maximal-set polynomial of this graph family. Injective-edge-coloring chromatic-index results count colors in partitions, not maximal individual color classes. Searches of exact problem, aliases, strongly covering parameters, and related published records found no statement implying the enumerator; this is provisional and not a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: Complete classification and full labeled polynomial solve a natural maximal-set enumeration problem for canonical one-subdivisions of complete graphs. The minimum \(n-1\), maximum \(\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor\), exact arithmetic cardinality spectrum, and even-only spectrum at odd n distinguish possible inclusion-maximal color-class sizes beyond the previously studied single maximum. These invariants support reproducible benchmark examples and are not merely renamings of the established maximum number.
